initiative.title: Orbit League: car ball in a spinning arena in orbit
initiative.body: Electric roadsters with rocket packs play three-a-side ball in a glass arena in orbit, where gravity is whatever the arena is spinning at. Pitched by Topher on the October 30, 2026 recording: "a racing game like Rocket League, but with Tesla Roadsters, in space." The cars, driver and badge are our own design; no carmaker's name, logo or trade dress.

milestones.title: First playable
milestones.body: A car, a ball and two goals you can play in the browser and on a phone at openagents.com/realms/orbit-league.

milestones.title: Pitch: one car, one ball, a goal in 1 g
milestones.body: Rigid-body contacts and the vehicle controller, so the car drives, jumps, dodges and boosts and hits the ball the same way every time. Offline.

milestones.title: Space: the drum arena, spin and zero-g
milestones.body: The ring-station drum arena, gravity from its spin, half spin, spin-down events, boost pads and driving on every surface.

milestones.title: Bots: 1v1 and 2v2 alone
milestones.body: Car-ball bots in plain code, so a match plays offline against the computer.

milestones.title: Online: quick match
milestones.body: A 60 Hz authoritative room with prediction and rollback, and a matchmaking queue per mode.

milestones.title: Show-off: replays, clips and car paint
milestones.body: Goal replays from three cameras, shareable clips, and colours and decals players make.

tasks.title: First playable at openagents.com/realms/orbit-league
tasks.body: The first version anyone can play: one roadster of our own design on a flat floor in 1 g, a two-metre ball and two goals. Drive, steer, jump, boost and hit the ball; a goal scores and resets the kickoff. Five-minute match clock and a score. Phone thumbs (left steers; JUMP and BOOST on the right) and keyboard. Offline, single player. Mark this done when the page plays.
acceptance: https://openagents.com/realms/orbit-league loads and plays: the car drives, jumps and boosts, and hitting the ball into a goal scores
The same page plays on a phone with on-screen thumbs
The realm is listed or linked from this project's page

tasks.title: Ball cam and the chase camera
tasks.body: A chase camera behind the car and a ball cam toggled with one button (on screen on a phone) that keeps the ball in view, blended with verse/camera.coax shots.
acceptance: Toggling ball cam keeps the ball on screen while the car drives away from it
The toggle works by key and by on-screen button

tasks.title: A goal explodes in the team's colour and knocks cars back
tasks.body: When the ball crosses a goal line: a particle burst in the scoring team's colour (verse/particles.coax), every car pushed back from the goal, a short pause, then kickoff positions.
acceptance: Scoring shows the burst and pushes the car back
Kickoff resets the ball to the centre and the car to its spot

tasks.title: Play the first version and write down what to fix
tasks.body: Play the first playable on a desktop browser and a phone for ten minutes each and post a note on this task with what feels wrong (car handling, hits, camera, thumbs), as new tasks where they are clear.
acceptance: A note on this task lists what was found on desktop and on phone
Each clear fix is a new task in this project

tasks.title: Contacts for rigid bodies: sphere, box and mesh, with friction and restitution
tasks.body: Add contacts to verse/rigid.coax: sphere against box, box against box (the car as an oriented box), sphere against mesh (the arena), with friction and restitution. Swept tests for the ball at speed so it never passes through a goal frame. Generalise Dead Gears' arena_sweep (verse/deadgears/arena.coax).
acceptance: coax test verse/rigid.coax passes with tests for each contact pair
A ball at 100 m/s fired at a goal post never passes through it in a test

tasks.title: A vehicle controller: wheels, suspension, grip, handbrake, jump, dodge
tasks.body: A new verse/vehicle.coax: four wheel rays, suspension springs, tyre grip, a handbrake drift, and sticky driving on walls and ceilings when the wheels touch and the car is fast enough. Jump, double jump and dodge impulses are fixed numbers so skill shots repeat exactly. Boost is a rear rocket that works in the air.
acceptance: coax test verse/vehicle.coax passes
The same inputs from the same start give the same car path bit for bit in a test

tasks.title: Hits take their direction from contact point, speed and spin
tasks.body: The ball's response to a car hit depends on where on the car it lands, the car's speed and spin, tuned so a front-flip shot and a side dodge feel distinct. The first playable moves onto the vehicle controller and contacts.
acceptance: A test hits the ball with the nose, a corner and the roof and gets three distinct directions
The realm uses verse/vehicle.coax

tasks.title: Gravity as a field, not a constant
tasks.body: Gravity points toward the drum's outer wall, scaled by spin. verse/player.coax and verse/throw.coax take a gravity function instead of a constant; existing realms keep their constant through it.
acceptance: Existing realms' tests still pass
A test drops a ball in a spinning drum and it falls toward the outer wall

tasks.title: The drum arena: a curved floor that becomes the walls and ceiling
tasks.body: The inside of a drum as the drivable surface and collision mesh, drawn in the flat or ink style (docs/verse/art-styles.md), with goals at each end.
acceptance: The car drives from the floor up the curve onto the ceiling at speed
The ball collides with the curved mesh in a test

tasks.title: Full spin, half spin and spin-down every 90 seconds
tasks.body: The station's spin sets gravity: full (about 1 g), half (about 0.4 g), and every 90 seconds a 15-second spin-down to zero g where every car gets a full boost tank. The interval is a setting so playtests can try 60 s, 90 s and off.
acceptance: A match shows a spin-down at 90 s lasting 15 s with full tanks
The interval setting changes it to 60 s or off

tasks.title: Boost pads on the floor and walls
tasks.body: Small and large boost pads placed on the arena floor and walls that refill boost when driven over and come back after a delay.
acceptance: Driving over a pad refills boost and the pad comes back after its delay

tasks.title: The sphere arena with goals at the poles
tasks.body: A second arena shape: a sphere with goals at the poles.
acceptance: The sphere arena is selectable and plays a full match

tasks.title: A car-ball bot that drives to an intercept and shoots at the goal
tasks.body: Plain code, no model calls: predict the ball, pick an intercept point, drive and jump to it and hit toward the opponent's goal; defend when the ball heads for its own goal.
acceptance: A bot scores against an empty goal in a test
A full 1v1 against a bot plays to the clock

tasks.title: 1v1 and 2v2 against bots, 2v2 the default
tasks.body: Pick a mode; bots fill every empty seat. 2v2 is the default for phones.
acceptance: Both modes start and finish with bots in every empty seat

tasks.title: A 60 Hz WebSocket room with the server's ball
tasks.body: A WebSocket room on the API with a 60 Hz server tick; the server owns the ball. Today's rooms are HTTP at five posts a second (coax/web/api/room.c).
acceptance: Two browsers in one room see the same ball
The server tick holds 60 Hz under four players in a load test

tasks.title: Prediction for your car, interpolation for others, rollback on correction
tasks.body: Client prediction for your own car through the deterministic vehicle controller, interpolation for other cars, and rollback when the server corrects.
acceptance: With 150 ms simulated latency your car responds at once and corrections don't snap visibly

tasks.title: Quick match: a queue per mode, bots fill empty seats
tasks.body: Matchmaking with a queue per mode; a match starts after a short wait with bots in any empty seat.
acceptance: Two players pressing QUICK MATCH land in the same match

tasks.title: Goal replays of the last five seconds from three cameras
tasks.body: Record inputs per tick and replay them through the same deterministic physics, as Ice Cream Man's trace and replay do (verse/icecream/). After a goal, the last five seconds play from three cameras.
acceptance: A replay of recorded inputs ends with the same ball position as the live match in a test

tasks.title: Shareable clips from replays
tasks.body: Save a replay as a link anyone can open and watch.
acceptance: A saved clip's link plays the same replay in another browser

tasks.title: Car colours and decals made by players
tasks.body: Pick a car colour and place decals players make; others see them online.
acceptance: A painted car shows the same paint to another player in a match

tasks.title: A car that rides up the glass comes back down on its wheels
tasks.body: Playtest #26ec: a car hitting the glass fast, or the bot after a kickoff hit, rides up the wall and stands on its nose or tail for seconds with its wheels on the glass, and the camera has to look down on it. Until the drum arena (ol-drum-arena) lets cars drive the walls, a car whose wheels touch a wall and not the floor should settle back onto the floor within a second, wheels down.
acceptance: A #test drives a car into the glass at speed at several angles, with and without boost: within 1.5 s it is on the floor with its wheels down
Played on a phone and a laptop, no car is seen standing on the glass

tasks.title: A bot a first-time player can beat
tasks.body: Playtest #26ec: the bot found the ball and scored twice in the first 10 seconds (fixed for the kickoff in 88b1ceda91: it no longer boosts in), and it still scores long shots in the first minute while a new player is learning to steer. Give it a reaction delay after each touch, an aim error that shrinks as the match goes on, and a top speed below yours without boost, so a first match is close.
acceptance: A #test plays a scripted novice (drive at the ball, no boost, no jumps) for five minutes against the bot: the bot scores no more than three goals
The bot still scores against a player who stands still

tasks.title: The bot in the drum gives a new player a first minute
tasks.body: Played on production (desktop and phone, ?arena=drum): the bot scores within the first five to seven seconds after the opening kickoff, before a new player has found the ball. In the box, orbitleague-sim.coax holds the bot to at most two goals in the first minute against scripted novices; the drum isn't simulated. Run the same novices in the drum and tune the bot's drum play (its miss, its recovery after a hit, its line up the curve) until they hold there too.
acceptance: orbitleague-sim.coax runs its novices in the drum too and holds there: at most two bot goals in the first minute, the still player still concedes
Played on production in the drum, the bot doesn't score in the first 15 seconds against a player who drives at the ball
